fields.meta_description: Describe your sales process and get sales automation for lead routing, follow-ups, deal alerts, and pipeline reports in your CRM. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Sales Automation From New Lead to Signed Deal
fields.hero_description: Describe how leads come in, who works them, and when a deal needs a nudge. Emergent builds the routing, follow-ups, deal alerts, and pipeline dashboard as code you own.
fields.features_heading: What Sales Automation Handles for Reps
fields.features_subheading: Sales automation runs the repetitive parts of selling: routing leads, sending follow-ups, and logging every touch to the CRM.
fields.feature_1:
Lead capture and instant routing

Demo requests, chat leads, and list uploads land in one table. Each lead is enriched, checked against the CRM for duplicates, and assigned by territory, size, or rotation.
fields.feature_2:
Follow-up sequences that stop on reply

Multi-step emails go out from each rep's own inbox on the days you set. A reply, a booked meeting, or an unsubscribe stops the sequence and records the outcome on the deal.
fields.feature_3:
Activity written back to the CRM

Emails, meetings, and call notes sync to Salesforce, HubSpot, or Pipedrive through their APIs. Every contact record shows the latest touch, and no rep has to type it in.
fields.feature_4:
Stalled deal and renewal alerts

A deal quiet for 14 days, a slipped close date, or a renewal 90 days out sends the owner an alert in Slack or email. The reminder repeats each morning until someone acts on it.
fields.feature_5:
Discount approvals in Slack

Discounts above your threshold go to a sales manager or finance in Slack, with deal size, term, and margin on the request. Each decision is logged against the opportunity.
fields.feature_6:
Your sales playbook, exported as code

Routing rules, sequences, and the pipeline dashboard export to your GitHub repository. Move a territory by prompting, or hand the code to your engineers to extend it.

fields.tab_content_1:
Route each inbound lead to the right rep while it is warm

Each demo request is checked against the CRM for an existing account, enriched with company size and region, and assigned to a rep by territory. The rep gets a Slack alert with the lead's details, and the owner is written back to the CRM.
fields.tab_content_2:
Follow up after every demo until the buyer replies

When a demo ends, the recap and next steps go out from the rep's inbox the same day. A second email follows on day 3. If there is still no reply by day 7, the rep gets a call task in Slack, and any reply stops the sequence.
fields.tab_content_3:
Catch quiet deals before the forecast call

Every open deal is checked each morning for days since the last touch. A deal quiet for 14 days is flagged on the pipeline dashboard and sent to its owner in Slack with the deal value. It gets a next step before Friday's forecast review.
fields.tab_content_4:
Start every renewal 90 days before the contract ends

Contract end dates are read from the CRM each week. Every account renewing in the next 90 days lands on its account manager's list with open tickets and the current price. The list posts to Slack each Monday, and a renewal opportunity is created in the CRM.

fields.howto_description: Write down how a lead becomes a deal on your team today. Routing, follow-ups, alerts, and reporting come from those rules, in seven steps from first touch to renewal.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Map how a lead becomes a customer
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write routing rules in plain English
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Connect your CRM, inbox and Slack
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every place leads come from: the demo form, chat, events, and outbound lists. Write down who owns each stage and where deals wait today. That map becomes the routing and the pipeline stages, so no lead sits unassigned.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Describe assignment the way your sales ops lead would: accounts with 200 or more employees go to the enterprise rep for that region, everything else rotates among the team. Emergent turns those sentences into rules you can read and change later.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide what happens after a demo, a no-show, and a stalled proposal: which emails go out, on which days, and when a person should call instead. Write the templates in your reps' voice, and let any reply stop the sequence.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, or any CRM with an API, plus Gmail or Outlook and Slack. Contacts, deals, and stages sync in. Owners, activity, and outcomes sync back, so the CRM stays the record your managers trust.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the few signals that deserve a rep's attention: a deal quiet for 14 days, a close date pushed twice, a renewal 90 days out. Each alert names the owner, the deal value, and the next step, and repeats until someone acts.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run a quarter of real leads and deals through the workflow before go-live. Check that every lead lands with the rep your team would have picked, adjust any rule that disagrees by prompting, and replay it until the two lists match.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Go live one lead source at a time
fields.howto_step_7_des: Turn routing on for the demo form first, then add chat and events. Watch time to first touch, reply rate, and quiet deals on the dashboard. When a number drifts, change the rule that drives it; each version is saved in your repo.
